name: umple
desc: Modeling tool/programming language that enables Model-Oriented Programming
why: A model-oriented programming language that blends UML modelling with code; an unusual paradigm worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Umple is a modeling tool and programming language family. It adds modeling abstractions such as associations, attributes and state machines to object-oriented languages (Java, Python, C++, PHP). It takes Umple text as input and generates code in those languages, along with diagrams, metrics and other artifacts. It can also produce many kinds of software engineering diagrams textually. It runs in a browser through UmpleOnline, or as a command-line jar, and has plugins for VS Code and other IDEs.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches Umple as a way to cut boilerplate: it claims a system takes far fewer lines than in a typical language, and that the generated boilerplate never has to be inspected or maintained because it is tested. It also positions Umple as a way to check AI-generated models, since you can read the Umple text and its diagrams.
brief.how_it_works: You write a class-level model in Umple syntax, such as classes with attributes and association lines like '* -- 1 Student;'. The compiler generates target-language code (Java, C++, PHP, and Python in beta per the README) with sensible default implementations for association link management, constructors and accessors. The homepage says the compiler is itself written in Umple and that Umple can be embedded in host-language code and vice versa.
brief.install_notes: Nothing needs installing to try it: UmpleOnline runs in the browser at try.umple.org, and a Docker image runs the GUI locally. For command-line use, download the Umple jar from the download page, which needs Java (8 or later, 17 recommended). The homepage also lists Homebrew (Mac/Linux), Chocolatey (Windows) and a Docker image under Downloads. The README mentions an Eclipse plugin and a developer setup wiki page. I did not see a specific brew command or a first-run walkthrough.
brief.standout: Umple's pitch is the reverse of most code generators: the model is the thing you edit and read, and the boilerplate is generated and treated as disposable. It also has a graphical editor where diagram elements map back to the Umple text. The README says the compiler is self-hosted, meaning Umple is written in Umple.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists a run of 2024 to 2026 feature news items, including a new Python generator, persistence changes and an LSP server. The README says releases come 1-4 times a year and describes active CI on Jenkins and AppVeyor. It has been on GitHub since 2015 and was first released in 2007. I did not see a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The README says the Python generator is beta; check the current status before relying on it. Java, C++ and PHP are the mature targets. Running locally needs Java. The README describes some subprojects as early development (for example the SDL generator). Much of the code is research-derived, so expect academic-project rough edges. The homepage was reachable, but the GitHub README was fetched from github.com/umple/umple, not from the homepage itself, because the homepage is not a repo URL.
quotes: Umple is a modeling tool and programming language family to enable what we call Model-Oriented Programming.
Umple creates reliable code from highly-readable abstractions.
the boilerplate never has to be inspected or maintained, and has been tested so that it is reliable.
The word 'Umple' is a play on words, meaning 'Simple', 'UML Programming Language' and 'Ample'.
fetch_log: https://cruise.umple.org/umple/ - worked; returned the homepage text, not a README. The README was thin on install and usage detail.
https://github.com/umple/umple - worked; returned the project README with install, license and directory details.
